biography: Naoki Hattori's racing journey began on the narrow, winding mountain roads outside Nagano, where he honed his skills drifting his father's old Toyota Celica. The thrill of pushing the car to its limit sparked a lifelong passion. He quickly rose through the ranks of Japanese domestic racing, earning a reputation as a fearless, if somewhat erratic, driver. A brief, unsuccessful stint in Formula 3000 exposed his inconsistency, but a surprise opportunity arose with McLaren F1 LM in a one-off endurance race. Despite initial promise, a late-race crash shattered his confidence and stalled his career. Now in his mid-thirties, Hattori finds himself bouncing between smaller GT series, his once-bright potential fading into the twilight of his career. He is seen as a talented driver past his prime, grasping at opportunities to prove he still has what it takes, but his inconsistent performances and sometimes volatile temper often undermine his efforts.
drivingStyle: Hattori possesses an aggressive, almost reckless driving style, characterized by late braking and a willingness to take risks in overtaking maneuvers. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also leads to frequent errors and collisions. His tire management is often poor, as he tends to overdrive the car in the early stages of a race, leading to significant performance drop-off later on. Under pressure, Hattori's inconsistency becomes even more pronounced; he is either brilliant or disastrous, with little in between.

careerHighlight: Winning the All-Japan Formula Three Championship in 1998, a dominant season showcasing his raw talent and potential.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 24 Hours of Le Mans while driving for McLaren F1 LM, costing the team a likely victory and severely damaging his reputation.
